text.91aa96869892ea9022f8: The evidence supports a durable, modest-growth ecosystem, but does not support extending the latest 16–17% revenue growth or 50.1% gross margin indefinitely. Keep a three-year explicit growth phase before fading to maturity. A base 9%/8%/7% revenue path, first-year 31% operating margin and eventual 32% margin is more informative than immediately fading a single starting rate. Apple's June gross-margin refund benefit and September memory-cost pressure pull near-term margin in opposite directions.
text.2f357b9c635c1c07bf84: Research judgment; management guidance and reported facts are linked separately.
text.ca1da90008e48c694fe0: Microsoft's demand and distribution evidence supports a longer growth phase than a mature software-only model, but the capital burden has changed fundamentally. Use five explicit early years in the base and bull cases, then a fade to maturity. Base revenue growth18%/17%/15%/13%/11% reaches approximately$661bn in year5 and$1.217tn in year15. That requires successful monetization and utilization, not simply a large order book.
text.169dc9b417f584c7b77b: AWS acceleration warrants an explicit three-year high-growth phase rather than fading growth immediately. It does not warrant valuing AI capacity as capital-light software. A proposed base is 18%, 17%, 15% revenue growth for years 1–3, then a fade to 2.5% by year 15, a 16% mature operating margin, 24% normalized tax, 10.25% WACC, and 12% terminal ROIC. Early sales/incremental-capital ratios of 0.65, 0.75 and 0.85 keep substantial build-out costs in the forecast.
text.ef47517c32c6608c5613: Cloud acceleration and TPU hardware deliveries justify a three-year explicit growth phase, but the business is becoming more capital-intensive and financially complex. Proposed base revenue growth is 22%, 20%, 18% in years 1–3, fading to 2.5% by year 15, with 32% mature operating margin, 22% normalized tax, 10% WACC and 16% terminal ROIC. Early sales/incremental-capital ratios are 0.50, 0.55 and 0.60, capturing capex and inventory pressure.
text.7c9c749532ababa47201: The core advertising franchise supports strong near-term growth, but the capital and legal commitments make a simple extrapolation of 2025 margins and free cash flow unreliable. Proposed base revenue growth is 20%, 18%, 16% in the first three forecast years, then a rate fade to 2.5% by year 10. The proposed mature EBIT margin is 33%, normalized tax 20%, direct early capital-spend/D&A/working-capital assumptions (derived S:C approximately 0.34, 0.36, 0.39, followed by normalization and a terminal-consistent transition), WACC 10%, and terminal ROIC 12%. These are our assumptions, not management forecasts. Forecast year one is the rolling year after June 2026, not calendar 2026. The claims bridge remains unresolved, so these are operating-value scenarios rather than finished share-price targets.
text.5ddbdca9543b14424c7e: The current operating ramp warrants a steeper early revenue path than the old flat 40% input, but financing support and supplier commitments now warrant an equally explicit downside model. The latest quarter was $96.221bn revenue, 106% year-over-year growth and $63.734bn GAAP operating income. Latest TTM revenue/EBIT were $302.970bn/$197.579bn. A low reported physical-capex ratio no longer captures the whole economic commitment.
text.18669224532832ba372a: Tesla requires an explicit capital-spending and contingent-dilution model before a renewed share-price default. The latest quarter's 26% revenue growth coexists with a 1.4% operating margin and more than $25bn planned 2026 capex. A base case of 12%, 12%, 10% initial growth and eventual 10% EBIT margin requires a recovery in vehicle economics and growth in energy/services; major Robotaxi or Optimus profits remain conditional. A constant sales-to-capital ratio cannot faithfully represent both the present buildout and later capital normalization.
text.2d904c702b7473eb9453: Annual revenue increased from $4,707.7m in FY2024 to $5,810.1m in FY2025 and $7,118.2m in FY2026. Latest-quarter revenue was $2,045.5m, up 33.8% year on year and 13.3% sequentially. Datacenter and Communications reached $5,274.6m for FY2026, approximately 74.1% of revenue, versus $3,755.2m a year earlier. Industrial declined to $1,843.6m from $2,055.0m, with portfolio sales affecting comparability. Treat AI optics as the principal current growth driver rather than extrapolating equal growth across both segments.
text.3d4a60f9f64bddb82bfb: Annual revenue was $1,359.2m in FY2024, $1,645.0m in FY2025 and $3,014.0m in FY2026. EBIT moved from losses of $434.0m and $180.1m to positive $524.8m. Q4 revenue reached $1,006.3m, up 109.3% year on year and 24.5% sequentially. Components contributed $649.4m and Systems $356.9m; the preceding quarter was $533.3m and $275.1m. Both product groups accelerated, rather than all growth being confined to one small pilot product.
text.ca21b52232edaf5bce31: Revenue grew from $217.6m in 2023 to $249.4m in 2024 and $455.7m in 2025. Operating losses were $41.3m, $70.9m and $54.6m respectively. Q2 2026 revenue of $191.922m compared with $102.952m a year earlier and $151.144m in Q1. Datacenter contributed $107.662m, CATV $80.578m, telecom $3.411m and other $0.271m. Datacenter is now about 56% of quarterly revenue; a single blended optical-growth assumption obscures CATV exposure and product-transition risk.
text.212ad5dc57961a60ed84: The Russian-business divestment in July 2024 and Toloka deconsolidation in 2025 make old Yandex growth and margins poor comparables. Recast continuing revenue was $91.5m in 2024 and $529.8m in 2025. The four 2025 quarters were $50.9m, $105.1m, $146.1m and $227.7m. Q1 2026 revenue reached $399.0m; Q2 reached $582.3m, with AI cloud contributing $574.9m, about 98% of group revenue. TripleTen and Avride remain in consolidated economics, while private investments require separate treatment.
text.29b0b70e543aec5c48d7: Preserve the reported FY2026 revenue of $133.188bn and GAAP EBIT of $99.340bn. They are real reported results, but an exceptional pricing-cycle endpoint. A flat 8% growth forecast from that annual base misses the much higher exit rate, while perpetuating the latest margin makes scarcity permanent. The preferred analytical base explicitly captures another boom year, then a price/capacity normalization in FY2029–2030. The date of normalization is a judgment, not management guidance.
text.c43fd1f2800c6efe0e27: Latest quarterly revenue was $29.591bn, up 86% year over year; GAAP EBIT $15.955bn, a 53.92% margin. Latest TTM revenue/EBIT were $89.104bn/$42.814bn. AI is accelerating far faster than the old undifferentiated 35% growth assumption, but memory pass-through, customer concentration and financing support make a simple high-margin extrapolation incomplete.
text.8e90d94bf7bfb442028c: TSMC's leading-node/advanced-packaging position and recent execution support strong near-term growth and longer persistence than a commodity-memory supplier. They do not justify compounding management's2024–2029 target for five fresh years from today. The preferred base starts with the TIFRS TTM revenue of TWD4.944817tr, models five explicit early years, and fades growth/returns across15 years. The base reaches46% EBIT margin,18% terminal ROIC and2% terminal growth, with capital intensity rising as growth matures.
